Guéhi made a costly error during last weekend’sdefeat by Spainand Anderson was off colour duringthe win over Czechialast Tuesday but Tuchel believes both are ready to start against Croatia on Saturday night.England are second in Group A3 with three points from two games. Jordan Pickford, who remains the No 1, will replace James Trafford in goal and Tuchel must decide whether to restore Jarell Quansah at right-back after Trent Alexander-Arnold shone against Czechia in Prague.Alexander-Arnold was an unused substitute when England drew in Rijeka in 2018. His place remains uncertain and Tuchel considered whether it was now or never for the Real Madrid defender, who turns 28 next week.“Maybe, maybe a little bit,” he said. “Once you are in camp it’s a big opportunity if other players are not here. Trent is a unique player. He is not a runner, he is not someone who runs through the last line, who does overlaps, underlaps.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenThomas Tuchel has said it ‘may be’ now or never for Trent Alexander-Arnold to win his place in the England team.Photograph: Antonio Bronić/ReutersTuchel explained that Alexander-Arnold is building a connection with Bukayo Saka. “Bukayo is normally used to a lot of movements around him,” he said. “That brings normally the best out of Bukayo. They need also to find a way to not be too static, to not be too ball-position focused and that we play with dynamic movement. That’s maybe the challenge for Trent: to buy a little bit into a new idea and a bit out of his comfort zone. He’s trying and it’s never too late to prove a point.”Tuchel is happy with Saka’s level. The Arsenal winger struggled with fitness during the World Cup but has been a regular for his club this season.“He had a strong start,” Tuchel said. “I could see he was pain-free. He had a bit of a strange ending to last season. He was playing through the pain, he was deciding matches but struggling to have big influence – and yet then having the biggest influence, by scoring decisive goals.“He scored decisive goals without being fit and without having the capability to accelerate and decelerate. Now I felt him more involved, and felt he was more dangerous at the start of the season – and still I think there is some level still to come when he plays for England.”Explore more on these topicsEnglandThomas TuchelManchester CitynewsShareReuse this content

title: Etihad’s statements on funding appear to contradict Manchester City’s defence | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Manchester City’s defence in their appeal against charges of financial rule breaches does not align with previous statements made by Etihad Airways
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Manchester City’s defence in their appeal against charges of financial rule breaches does not align with previous statements made by Etihad Airways
Content: Manchester City’s owner Sheikh Mansour (centre) and chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak (right).Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAView image in fullscreenManchester City’s owner Sheikh Mansour (centre) and chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak (right).Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAManchester CityEtihad’s statements on funding appear to contradict Manchester City’s defenceAirline denied links to Abu Dhabi government in 2015FA confirms it has powers to take disciplinary actionMatt HughesFri 2 Oct 2026 13.58 EDTFirst published on Fri 2 Oct 2026 05.15 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleManchester City’s defence in their appeal against theindependent commission’s guilty verdictin more than 100 charges of financial rule breaches appears to be contradicted by previous statements made by their main sponsor, Etihad Airways, to the US government.A key element of City’s appeal, which was confirmed by the club on Friday, is understood to be based on their claim that commercial contracts, which the commission concluded were part-funded by their owner, were in fact paid for by the Abu Dhabi government.Criminal or saviour? Rui Pinto abandoned by Portuguese authorities after Manchester City leaksRead moreIn a 2015 submission to the United States’ department of commerce, transportation and state as part of investigation into state-owned airlines, Etihad described suggestions that the government paid for its sponsorship of the club as “false”.Etihad, the state-owned national airline of the United Arab Emirates, has been City’s principal shirt sponsor since 2009 and was the main source of the initial transformation of their revenue that followed their purchase by Sheikh Mansour’s Abu Dhabi United Group (Adug) the previous year.In 2011 City announced a 10-year naming rights deal worth £400m for the Etihad Stadium, which was extended on improved terms in 2021.The Etihad submission to the US department of commerce said: “The assertion that the Abu Dhabi government paid for Etihad’s sponsorship of English Premier League football clubManchester Cityis false. In 2011, Etihad and Manchester City entered into a 10-year sponsorship agreement, which included naming rights for Manchester City’s stadium. Etihad funded this sponsorship from its own liquidity.“We are government-owned and have been since our founding. We are and have always been clear that we do not receive any subsidies from the Abu Dhabi government, and that we are financed through a combination of equity, shareholder and commercial loans.“Our shareholder [the Abu Dhabi government]’s equity and loans are not subsidies under any applicable definition; they are the means by which the Abu Dhabi government has sensibly invested in a successful business model.”Andy Burnham urged by Lib Dems to reveal all meetings with owners of Manchester CityRead moreCity’s argument is also a departure from the position the club took in theirsuccessful appeal against Uefa’s chargesof breaching financial fair play rules at the court of arbitration for sport in 2020, when they maintained that all their sponsorship income was provided by their commercial partners.The commission dismissed City’s argument as “untrue” in its core decision published on Tuesday. Paragraph 77 of the judgment states: “We concluded that it was an ‘explanation’ that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the realities of the Disguised Funding Scheme.” City submitted their appeal on Thursday evening and insist they have “a body of irrefutable evidence” that will prove the commission’s findings to be untrue.The Football Association has confirmed it has powers to take disciplinary action against City and key individuals at the club.The FAsaid the independent commission’s decision on City had “significant implications for the integrity of the game” and that it “will take action where appropriate”.The FA will wait until the appeal process has concluded – which based on the Premier League’s rule book should be by the end of January – before deciding whether to take action but said it was monitoring the case closely.The FA has powers to take action against individuals proved to have broken rules and/or acted dishonestly, which the commission concluded had been the case. The names of those involved were redacted in the 40-page core judgment published this week but the FA could ask the Premier League for an unredacted version.“The Independent Commission’s decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game,” the FA statement read. “We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“As proceedings between the Premier League and Manchester City Football Club remain ongoing, we do not intend to comment further at this stage. We will, however, continue to monitor developments closely.”The FA’s standard practice is to wait for disciplinary proceedings conducted by leagues, such as the Premier League or EFL, to run their course before taking action.In July theFA fined Chelsea £10mand imposed a suspended two-window transfer ban after the club admitted 74 breaches of its agent regulations, four months after thePremier League fined them £10.75mfor the same offences, which related to unlawful payments to players and agents. The FA has additional powers to take action against individuals, although did not do so in the Chelsea case because those involved are no longer working in football.The FAcharged Southampton’s manager, Tonda Eckert, with misconduct for his role in the so-called Spygate saga involving Middlesbrough in May, with a disciplinary hearing taking place last month that could result in the German being given a lengthy ban from football.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityThe FAFinancesFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Nations League: Italy earn draw against 10-man France, Northern Ireland stun Ukraine | Nations League | The Guardian
description: Italy denied Zinedine Zidane victory in his first France home game while Northern Ireland boosted their promotion bid with victory in Trnava
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Italy denied Zinedine Zidane victory in his first France home game while Northern Ireland boosted their promotion bid with victory in Trnava
Content: Italy celebrate Alessandro Bastoni’s equaliser as Roberto Mancini’s side spoiled the party at Stade de France.Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/DPPI/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenItaly celebrate Alessandro Bastoni’s equaliser as Roberto Mancini’s side spoiled the party at Stade de France.Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/DPPI/ShutterstockNations LeagueNations League: Italy earn draw against 10-man France, Northern Ireland stun UkraineLeague A: France 1-1 Italy, Belgium 3-0 TurkeyNorthern Ireland boost promotion bid with 3-0 winAgencies andGuardian sportFri 2 Oct 2026 17.11 EDTLast modified on Fri 2 Oct 2026 19.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleZinedine Zidane’s first home game in charge ofFranceended with a 1-1 draw againstItalyin theNations Leagueon Friday. Visiting keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma produced a string of saves to frustrate fans at Stade de France, while the hosts ended the game with 10 men after Dayot Upamecano’s late dismissal.France 1-1 Italy: Nations League football – live reactionRead moreMichael Olise putFranceahead in the 55th minute with a curling shot that went in off the crossbar, following a short free-kick taken by Rayan Cherki. But poor defending midway through the second half allowed Italy defender Alessandro Bastoni to run through and clip a low shot inside the right post.Moise Kean missed a close-range chance early on forItaly, shooting straight at goalkeeper Mike Maignan. Donnarumma made a double save from Ousmane Dembélé and Désiré Doué early in the second half, then produced a brilliant low save to deny Adrien Rabiot moments after Italy’s equaliser.Upamecano was sent off late in the game for picking up a second yellow card, but the hosts kept pushing for a winner, and Donnarumma had to claw away Eduardo Camavinga’s shot in stoppage time to preserve a point.“We would have liked to win for our fans tonight but I was obviously really touched and delighted to be back at the Stade de France,” Zidane said afterwards. “I am happy with the performance albeit not with the result. We had chances to score a second goal and we didn’t do it. But I am really proud of my players.”The Italy manager, Roberto Mancini, was pleased with his side’s efforts. “I think this was a great performance tonight against one of the best teams in the world, with very positive aspects to it,” he said. “We are on the right road, and we need to keep playing this way.”Francestay top of Group A1, a point clear ofBelgiumwho eased to a 3-0 home win over bottom sideTurkeyin Liège. The two neighbours meet again on Monday at the Stade de France, while Italy host Turkey in Bologna.View image in fullscreenKevin De Bruyne celebrates after scoring one of his two goals for Belgium in Liège.Photograph: Virginie Lefour/Belga/ShutterstockKevin De Bruyne, in his 127th match for the Red Devils, scored the opening goal with a cool finish from the edge of the box, after a nice one-two with Dodi Lukebakio. Turkey posed the greater attacking danger after the Napoli midfielder’s opener but could not find a leveller and were punished just before the hour mark.De Bruyne claimed his second goal in the 59th minute, curling a ball from the edge of the box past Turkey goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir into the top corner. Romelu Lukaku, Belgium’s all-time record goalscorer, added a third in the 76th minute, skewing the ball home from Charles De Ketelaere’s low cross.In League B,Northern IrelandstunnedUkraine3-0 in Slovakia to go clear at the top of their group and boost their hopes of promotion to the top tier.Ciaron Brown, the only player in Michael O’Neill’s starting lineup over the age of 24, scored twice either side of Isaac Price’s goal in Trnava. The away win puts Northern Ireland on seven points from three games, and they are still yet to concede going into Monday’s clash with Georgia in Belfast.Northern Ireland’s positive start was quickly rewarded as Kieran Morrison floated a corner to the back post where Ruairi McConville headed it back for Brown, earning his 33rd cap, to prod home despite the desperate efforts of Illia Zabarnyi on the line.View image in fullscreenCiaron Brown (left, No 22) celebrates his second goal of the night in Trnava.Photograph: Dénes Erdős/APGeorgiy Sudakov was the first Ukraine player to get a sight of goal but his 19th-minute effort was straight at keeper Pierce Charles, and moments later the hosts were 2-0 down. Morrison’s first-time ball into the box was met powerfully by Price at the back post – earning Morrison an assist in his first competitive international.Brown’s second came in bizarre fashion just after the hour – the 28-year-old Oxford defender went up to flick on Pierce Charles’ free-kick from inside the Northern Ireland half, and Ukraine goalkeeper Dmytro Riznyk let the bouncing ball slip through his legs to wrap up a remarkable result.“It’s a great result for us, a great performance,” O’Neill said. “The early goal helps settle us into the game. The second goal was a brilliant goal. We worked it the length of the pitch. We were patient. We could have crossed it early but that allowed us to get more men in the box and it’s a brilliant header from Isaac.“The third goal is fortuitous but it’s a mistake by the opposition, so we have to capitalise on that, but I thought throughout our performance was brilliant,” the Northern Ireland manager added. “We limited the opposition to crosses and shots from outside the box and I thought we defended brilliantly.”The Liverpool full-back Milos Kerkez scored the only goal in the other Group B2 tie to earnHungarya 1-0 win overGeorgia, moving the Magyars level with Ukraine in second place with four points from three games.Edin Dzeko brought the curtain down on his international career duringBosnia and Herzegovina’s 1-1 draw withSweden. The 40-year-old was withdrawn after 63 minutes of his 152nd appearance, with the hosts trailing after Viktor Gyökeres had scored two minutes earlier. Kerim Alajbegovic ensured the spoils would be shared with an 80th-minute effort.In the group’s other game,PolandthumpedRomania6-0 with Robert Lewandowski hitting a hat-trick. Radu Dragusin was sent off in the 22nd minute for bringing Lewandowski down in the area, and the veteran striker got up to convert the penalty. Lewandowski struck again in the 47th and 86th minutes, with Piotr Zielinski, Jan Bednarek and a Virgil Ghita own goal completing the scoring in Warsaw.View image in fullscreenRobert Lewandowski scores from the penalty spot to kick off Poland’s 6-0 rout of Romania.Photograph: Marek Antoni Iwańczuk/NurPhoto/ShutterstockTheFaroe Islandsearned an impressive 1-1 home draw with Group C3 leadersSlovakia, Adrian Justinussen’s second-half goal cancelling out a Gunnar Vatnhamar own goal before the break.Moldovamoved up to second in the group with a 2-1 away victory overKazakhstan.Elsewhere in the third tier, Vasilije Adzic scored twice as Group C2 leadersMontenegrowon 2-1 inLatvia, whileCyprusbeatArmenia2-0 despite a second-half red card for Kostas Pileas.Explore more on these topicsNations LeagueFranceItalyBelgiumNorthern IrelandnewsShareReuse this content

title: Arsenal shelve plans for major expansion of Emirates Stadium | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: Arsenal have shelved plans for a major expansion of the Emirates Stadium, opting for a programme of smaller improvements in hospitality, retail and matchday experience
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Arsenal have shelved plans for a major expansion of the Emirates Stadium, opting for a programme of smaller improvements in hospitality, retail and matchday experience
Content: Arsenal had considered expanding the size of the Emirates Stadium, but have instead opted for a range of smaller improvements.Photograph: Andrew Matthews/PAView image in fullscreenArsenal had considered expanding the size of the Emirates Stadium, but have instead opted for a range of smaller improvements.Photograph: Andrew Matthews/PAArsenalArsenal shelve plans for major expansion of Emirates StadiumClub opt for improvements in hospitality and retailAn increase to 60,704 capacity had been consideredEd AaronsFri 2 Oct 2026 16.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleArsenal have shelved plans for a major expansion of the Emirates Stadium, opting for a programme of smaller improvements as the club’s owners review the Premier League champions’ wider operation.Arsenal set up a working group led by the chief executive, Richard Garlick, in 2024 to examine the feasibility of increasing the 60,704 capacity, with some reports they could temporarily hold home matches at Wembley. But the club has decided against major redevelopment and will concentrate on what it described as the “continued evolution” of their home since 2006.Have Arsenal been figured out? Three big questions after Brighton’s upsetRead moreArsenal confirmed at a supporters’ meeting that improvements would focus on hospitality, retail, visitor facilities and the matchday experience – an area the co-chair Josh Kroenke previously highlighted.“We shared a commitment to the continued evolution of Emirates Stadium, rather than a huge-scale masterplan, building on improvement we have made to date in partnership with our catering partner, Legends, the introduction of safe standing (this season in the Clock End, and next season in the North Bank), improving hospitality and retail experiences, and upgrading visitor experiences,” Arsenal said.Mikel Arteta, who last season guided Arsenal to their first Premier League title since 2022, is believed to have expressed concern over the disruption that would have been caused by any temporary move. It is understood Arsenal did not apply to host matches at Euro 2028, with a potential redevelopment in mind.The club’s owner, Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, which agreed a record $4bn deal to buy Major League Baseball’s Los Angeles Angels last month, is understood to have brought in Boston Consulting Group (BCG) to examine parts of the operations. The review is understood to be overseen internally by Garlick and to be ongoing.There is no indication the review will necessarily result in job losses among Arsenal’s approximately 800 employees. Sources have suggested the work is principally focused on non-football operations and identifying ways to improve efficiency.The decision over the Emirates comes amid competition from Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, which opened in 2019 with a capacity of 62,850 and was designed to host a wide range of sporting and entertainment events, including NFL games and concerts. Arsenal, despite a smaller capacity, have significantly increased their matchday revenue. Income has reportedly doubled over five seasons to more than £150m a season, helped by the club’s return to the Champions League and an expansion of corporate hospitality.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe Arsenal Supporters’ Trust said it had been given guarantees the club had “no current plans” to reduce ordinary seating or move fans to increase corporate numbers.Christos Tzolis is to return to Arsenal for assessment after sustaining a suspected muscle injury with Greece. Germany’s Kai Havertz pulled out of international duty after picking up an injury against the Netherlands but Arsenal are believed to be hopeful he could feature against Leeds next Saturday.Explore more on these topicsArsenalnewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto to leave Portugal over safety fears | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Rui Pinto has had his witness protection status removed but his lawyers said they will appeal and that his situation is ‘critical’
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Rui Pinto has had his witness protection status removed but his lawyers said they will appeal and that his situation is ‘critical’
Content: Rui Pinto’s lawyers said he is ‘more vulnerable than at any point since 2020’.Photograph: Thomas Samson/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRui Pinto’s lawyers said he is ‘more vulnerable than at any point since 2020’.Photograph: Thomas Samson/AFP/Getty ImagesManchester CityManchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto to leave Portugal over safety fearsPinto has witness protection status removedHis lawyers will appeal and say his situation is ‘critical’Ed AaronsFri 2 Oct 2026 15.43 EDTLast modified on Fri 2 Oct 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRui Pinto has revealed he is preparing to leave Portugal because he fears for his safety after being informed that his participation in the country’s witness protection programme has been terminated.The Football Leaks founder claimed he has received “multiple death threats” and is facing “the serious risk of an assassination attempt against me” after being informed of the decision by Portuguese authorities on Wednesday. That came two days afterManchester City were found guilty of 115 chargesby an independent commission – an investigation that was prompted by Pinto’s leaks of thousands of private documents.Criminal or saviour? Rui Pinto abandoned by Portuguese authorities after Manchester City leaksRead moreHe said in a statement on Friday that the timing and circumstances of the decision to end his witness protection had left him facing a serious threat to his safety. “On 30 September 2026, just hours after the verdict officially confirming Manchester City’s guilt, the commission responsible for Portugal’s witness protection programme informed me of its decision to terminate my participation in the programme and withdraw my police protection, thereby knowingly placing me in a life-threatening situation,” he wrote on X.“Given these circumstances, I have no alternative but to relocate, within the next few days, to an undisclosed location for an indefinite period of time, due to the multiple death threats I have received and the serious risk of an assassination attempt against me. For this reason, I have just set up a GoFundMe campaign and I am asking for everyone’s support to help me survive this serious situation created by the Portuguese state, which, as I have already stated, has knowingly decided to place my life at risk.”TheGoFundMe campaign’s target has been set at €3m(£2.55m) and had received €4,000 in the first half-hour after it was posted. “I would like to take this opportunity to extend a special thanks to everyone who continues to support Football Leaks, and I can give everyone one guarantee: the fight will most certainly continue,” Pinto added.Earlier, the 37-year-old’s lawyers confirmed that they will appeal against the decision that was taken by the Portuguese authorities and said ending his protection would leave him “more vulnerable than at any point since 2020”. They argued that it was taken without giving him an opportunity to be heard and have described the circumstances surrounding it as a “failure to respect the rule of law”.How best to punish City? Restitution over retribution, then hand club to the fans | Jonathan LiewRead moreIn a request to Portugal’s Ministry of Justice, the lawyers asked the government to reconsider the decision, disclose the material on which the latest risk assessment was based and ensure that his protection continues.“His situation is now critical,” said his lawyers in a statement. “The threats against him are not merely theoretical: last April, he was assaulted in Lisbon. His revelations implicated powerful individuals with substantial resources, and many of the resulting legal proceedings are still ongoing, as demonstrated by the decision issued just a few days ago by the Premier League’s independent commission concerning Manchester City. Abruptly deprived of his protected residence and placed in a situation of extreme precariousness, Rui Pinto will now be more vulnerable than at any point since 2020.”Pinto entered Portugal’s protection programme after cooperating with the country’s justice authorities. His revelations have subsequently been used by judicial, tax and sporting authorities across Europe, including the Premier League’s investigation into City’s alleged financial irregularities. Pinto’s lawyers argue that the authorities should take into account both his cooperation with the justice system and the continuing risks associated with his disclosures before ending his protection.“This decision, and the manner in which it was taken, regrettably fail to respect the rule of law and constitute an act of state terrorism. We cannot accept this,” they added.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityPremier LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Slegers feels support from Arsenal hierarchy despite dismal run but biggest test looms | Arsenal Women | The Guardian
description: Renée Slegers said the board has been ‘really good and positive’ at a ‘difficult time’ as the team prepare to visit WSL leaders Manchester City on Sunday
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Renée Slegers said the board has been ‘really good and positive’ at a ‘difficult time’ as the team prepare to visit WSL leaders Manchester City on Sunday
Content: Renée Slegers (left) has overseen only one win in five matches and Arsenal have slipped seven points behind WSL leaders Manchester City.Photograph: Martin Rickett/Ben Whitley/PAView image in fullscreenRenée Slegers (left) has overseen only one win in five matches and Arsenal have slipped seven points behind WSL leaders Manchester City.Photograph: Martin Rickett/Ben Whitley/PAArsenal WomenSlegers feels support from Arsenal hierarchy despite dismal run but biggest test loomsBoard ‘really good and positive’ at ‘difficult time’Gunners visit WSL leaders Manchester City on SundayTom GarryFri 2 Oct 2026 12.38 EDTLast modified on Fri 2 Oct 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRenée Slegers says she has felt the full support of Arsenal’s board and praised her senior players for showing “monumental leadership” this week as she vows to find solutions to recent poor form before Sunday’s pivotal trip to Manchester City.One win in five matches has put Slegers under mounting pressure. Arsenal let slip a two-goal leadto draw at Paris FCin the Women’s ­Champions League on Wednesday and in the WSL they have slipped seven points behind City, the ­leaders and defending champions, having scored only twice in their four league games.Shaw secures WCL draw against Real Madrid as Manchester City show spirit after week of turmoilRead moreSlegers was in a determined mood on Friday, speaking of a “strong togetherness” at the club. Asked whether she felt the full support of the board, she replied: “Yes, that’s what I felt. That’s been positive and that’s helped me. The club’s leadership has been really good and positive for me in this moment because everyone thinks this is a difficult time and this is not something that we want for the team and for the club.“But the leadership from Clare [Wheatley, the director of football], Rich [Garlick, CEO], James [King, director of football operations], Jodie [Taylor, technical director] has been superb. So I want to give everything back to the club.“There’s been a lot of contact, of course. There’s a strong­togetherness and I’ve really felt their support and they’re here with us, which I’m very grateful for, of course, because I care so much for the team, for the club. I believe in the potential that we ­possess. I believe we can come out of this.”The 37-year-old Dutchwoman began with an apology to the media for her no-show after Wednesday’s game, whenArsenal conceded a bizarre penaltyafter Leah Williamson was penalised for handling the ball in the area when she thought she was taking a goal-kick. Slegers’s assistant Aaron D’Antino stepped in.PosTeamPGDPts1Man City Women48122Tottenham Hotspur Women413103Chelsea Women48104London City Lionesses4595Liverpool FC Women4476Everton Women4-167Arsenal Women4058Crystal Palace Women4-659Man Utd Women4-5410West Ham Women4-3311Brighton & Hove Albion Women4-3212Birmingham City Women4-4213Aston Villa Women4-7214Charlton Women4-90“After the game there was emotion from my end,” Slegers said. “[I] make the decision to be with the team instead.” She said that had felt important but added: “I will be there next time. I said to the team: ‘I’m angry, I’m really angry, and let’s try to use the emotions that we’re feeling and let it fuel us moving forward, so that’s definitely part of what I hope [to see] and what I believe is going to help us in the right direction.”Sunday presents a huge challenge against a side who have a 100% record in the WSL this season and have won all their home league matches since Andrée Jeglertz took over as head coach in the summer of 2025.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSlegers praised her squad for their response since Wednesday, saying her “players have been brilliant – I’ve seen the best sides of them”.“What the group has shown, it’s something I haven’t seen before,” she said. “The captains in the team they’ve been monumental; it’s the strongest leadership I’ve seen so far working within football, they’ve been amazing. They’re very calm, composed, solution-orientated and laser-focused. It was a great moment and I think vital for us moving forward.“It’s strange because I have to be finding a solution, so I have to be calm, I have to give direction, I have to lead now. But at the same time, what I also feel is gratitude for how everyone is responding and how together we are and how the session on the pitch was today. It was really, really good.”Explore more on these topicsArsenal WomenWomen's Super LeagueWomen's footballnewsShareReuse this content

title: Robbie Savage steps up to take Peterborough job: ‘All I want is a chance’ | Peterborough | The Guardian
description: Peterborough United have confirmed the appointment of Robbie Savage as their new manager, with the Welshman leaving his role at Forest Green to take up the position
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Peterborough United have confirmed the appointment of Robbie Savage as their new manager, with the Welshman leaving his role at Forest Green to take up the position
Content: Robbie Savage says ‘nobody’s given me anything in this world, I’ve earned it and I’ve worked hard for it’.Photograph: Craig Galloway/ProSports/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenRobbie Savage says ‘nobody’s given me anything in this world, I’ve earned it and I’ve worked hard for it’.Photograph: Craig Galloway/ProSports/ShutterstockPeterboroughRobbie Savage steps up to take Peterborough job: ‘All I want is a chance’Savage leaves Forest Green to take League One role‘Excitement is the word I can use,’ say MacAnthonyPress AssociationFri 2 Oct 2026 08.11 EDTLast modified on Fri 2 Oct 2026 10.51 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRobbie Savage has been confirmed as the new manager of League One strugglersPeterborough.Savage has lefthis role at National League side Forest Green Roversand signed a long-term contract at Posh, who are currently second from bottom and sacked Luke Williams last month. His appointment marks his first Football League rolesince retiring as a player in 2011, and Savage said he is relishing the opportunity to prove any doubters wrong.“Everyone’s entitled to their opinion but all I want is a chance. I’ve done it all my life,” Savage said. “When I was released by Manchester United I was told I wasn’t good enough, when I moved to Leicester I wasn’t in the team and had to battle. Nobody’s given me anything in this world, I’ve earned it and I’ve worked hard for it.“Judge me when we start playing football – that’s what I love. I’m passionate and emotional and I just want to watch this young team give me everything, play that explosive style of football.”Savage started his managerial career at Macclesfield, whom he steered to promotion to National League North before moving to Forest Green in 2025. He is expected to meet the players for the first time on Sunday before taking charge for in Tuesday’s Football League Trophy tie against Ipswich Under-21s.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The Peterborough chair, Darragh MacAnthony, said: “Excitement is the word I can use to describe the appointment of Robbie Savage as our new manager – a word I personally haven’t used about our football club for too long. His personality, character and mindset is something we need top to bottom. Nobody will work harder to get us up and running again than Robbie. The board were blown away by him in an extensive interview, and his hunger to fix our issues and get confidence back into our talented squad is what I am most excited by.”Explore more on these topicsPeterboroughLeague OneForest Green RoversnewsShareReuse this content

title: Bath go top with Finn Russell to the fore in thrilling derby victory against Exeter | Prem Rugby | The Guardian
description: Bath went to the top of the Gallagher Prem after beating Exeter Chiefs 40-34 in a pulsating West Country derby at the Rec
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Bath went to the top of the Gallagher Prem after beating Exeter Chiefs 40-34 in a pulsating West Country derby at the Rec
Content: Bernard van der Linde goes over to score one of Bath’s six tries in a thrilling match of 11 tries.Photograph: David Davies/PAView image in fullscreenBernard van der Linde goes over to score one of Bath’s six tries in a thrilling match of 11 tries.Photograph: David Davies/PAPrem RugbyBath go top with Finn Russell to the fore in thrilling derby victory against ExeterPrem Rugby: Bath 40-34 ExeterHosts made to fight all the way in 11-try thrillerPress AssociationFri 2 Oct 2026 17.31 EDTLast modified on Fri 2 Oct 2026 19.36 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBath went to the top of the Prem after beatingExeterChiefs in a pulsating West Country derby at the Rec but they were made to fight all the way in an 11-try thriller.Exeter trailed 26-10 at the interval but rallied to lead 33-31 midway through the second half before a yellow card for scrum-half Stephen Varney eventually proved decisive.‘They said I ran away from rucks’: Emmanuel Iyogun on going from reluctant prop to England debutRead moreCam Redpath, Dan du Preez, Bernard van der Linde, Ted Hill and Finn Russell scored Bath’s tries. There was also a penalty try award with Russell converting four. The hugely impressive Immanuel Feyi-Waboso scored two tries for Exeter, with Jack Yeandle, Josh Iosefa-Scott and Varney also going over. Henry Slade converted three and Harvey Skinner added a late penalty.Bath’s director of rugby, Johann Van Graan, was delighted with another five points. “We wanted to start well and achieved this to build up a healthy first-half lead but they went on to dominate the third quarter,” he said.“We then brought on our bench and obviously they made a big impact, so we finished strongly to get a valuable five points. It was particularly pleasing to see Jaco Coetzee back in action. He’s been out for nearly two years and he and Will Stuart, who also returned, made a big impact.“One scrum in the first half was huge as we shunted them backwards. It was a big momentum shift as we went to the corner and scored from there.”Rob Baxter, Exeter’s director of rugby, said: “I’m massively pleased with our intent and physicality as we turned up for the fight from the start. Even though we were 16 points down at the interval, I thought we were unlucky to be in that position.“It wasn’t against the run of play, but two of their tries came from when we were attacking with favourable bounces going their way. It was a massive step forward from last week’s disappointing effort and gives us a foundation to move on.”Bath took control as first Redpath intercepted a Skinner pass to run 50m and score before Van der Linde slipped through a gap in the visitors’ defence for an individual try. Russell converted both to give his side a 14-0 lead at the end of the first quarter.Exeter responded thanks to the strong running of Feyi-Waboso. First he evaded a tackle from Ollie Lawrence to put the defence on the back foot and when the ball was recycled he powered past another two coverers with Varney on hand to touch down.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenHenry Slade is tackled by Finn Russell, who was in the thick of the action for Bath.Photograph: Rachel Le Poidevin/PPAUK/ShutterstockThe hosts scored their third try when they capitalised on a favourable bounce on halfway. Van der Linde and Ewan Richards took advantage to give Du Preez the chance to force his way over from close range, but Bath bungled the kick-off so Yeandle was able to keep his side in contention with a try from a driving lineout.However, with half-time approaching, Bath exerted a period of pressure that culminated in Russell dummying his way over for the bonus-point try before converting for a 26-10 interval lead.Exeter began the second half strongly and were rewarded with two tries in quick succession. First Iosefa-Scott crashed over from close range before Feyi-Waboso took his opportunity in style by brushing aside two would-be tacklers. Slade converted both and his side were right back in it with just two points between the teams.Exeter took the lead for the first time when former Bath player Will Butt carved the hosts apart to provide Feyi-Waboso with an easy run-in for his second try. The home side were soon awarded a penalty try with Varney given a yellow card for a deliberate knock-on and in the scrum-half’s absence, Hill battered his way over.Slade missed badly with a penalty attempt so Skinner took over the goal-kicking and his success gave Chiefs two deserved bonus points from the match.Explore more on these topicsPrem RugbyBathExeterRugby unionnewsShareReuse this content
